cells.tense: The patience you spent is over and the yield of it is here to be looked at.
cells.act: keep your own count of what is owed, and pay it
cells.ask: Go back over the debts and favors still open between you and the people close to you, and settle the ones that are yours to settle — no explanation owed to anyone.
cells.core:
Something grew because you stayed with it long enough, and it is here now, in a shape you can pick up. You can look at what came of it without tallying every exchange that got you here. You know what is fair in this, and you act on it, and that is the ground you are standing on.

So go back over what is still open — the debts, the favors, the turns half-returned. Settle the ones that belong to you. It does not need a conversation with anyone, and it does not need to be talked about at all.

What you made is real, and it is allowed to leave your hands.
cells.sheetLine: Settle what is yours to settle, and the rest can go quiet.
cells.verb: Surveying what the change has actually grown
cells.place: In the room where everything is finished enough to leave

cells.tense: You are counting the next crop while this one is still standing in the field.
cells.act: sit with what the heart already knows
cells.ask: Take one unhurried stretch with something you have already made — no list, no next move, nothing to decide about it, and no clock running.
cells.core:
There are people in this room and you are ahead of them, tallying what the yield will mean before it has finished coming in. Gathering is your strength; doing it early is what runs past the point where anything can be stayed with. You feel the pull to decide what it all adds up to before it has arrived.

Sit with what your heart already knows instead. Take one unhurried stretch with something you have made — no list, no next move, nothing to settle, no clock running on it. Let the feeling be there without putting it to work. It does not need an outcome from you.

What you are rushing is your own harvest.

cells.tense: The last day of this passed while you were still standing near the door you left open.
cells.act: do the next piece at the speed you can keep for a month, not the speed you can keep for a day
cells.ask: Take the piece of finishing that has been sitting untouched and move it at a pace you could hold for a month — then stop when the month's pace says to.
cells.core:
What was grown has already been brought in, and you are back at the field, turning over what it took and what you would have done differently. Nothing is being gathered now. The hours that could go into this have been going into looking back at it, and what you spent so long on is running down while you stand there.

Move one piece of the finish at a pace you could keep for a month rather than a day. That is steady enough to start with. When the month's pace says to stop, stop.

There is a next thing, and it does not need the old field dug up first.

cells.tense: What holds this finished thing together was set by your hand, and you call it how it happens to be.
cells.act: declare the shape of it outward, plainly
cells.ask: Put into words what you decided about how this should be arranged, and that the decision was yours — out loud, or written where anyone could read it.
cells.core:
Something is settled here, and it is settled because you arranged it that way. Ask how it ended up this shape and the answer would be about what needed doing, what was obvious from the start. You have been holding the order of this thing steady so that people can move inside it, and you have not been saying that you are the one holding it.

Put the shape of it into the open. Say what you decided and that it came from you, out loud or written where anyone could read it, in your own words. The structure stays reliable either way. The person who set it would just be visible in what they made.

Being steady and being unseen are two different jobs.
